title: users rarely change defaults
rule: Users rarely change defaults — pick most common/safe, not first-alpha; don’t always default the most expensive.
pass_when: Default is the common or safe value, not alphabetical-first and not automatically the most expensive.
fail_when: First-alpha or most-expensive default with no common/safe basis.
overview: Defaults should be common or safe, not first-alpha or most expensive.
apply_when: Setting preselected values users are unlikely to change.
not_when: First-alphabetical or most-expensive defaults without a common or safe basis.
agent_hint: Default to the common or safe value; avoid first-alpha and auto most-expensive.
description: Users rarely change defaults, so pick the most common or safe value—not first-alphabetical and not automatically the most expensive. Pass when the default is the common or safe value on that basis. Fail when the default is first-alpha or most-expensive with no common or safe basis for the choice, biasing people toward a poor selection.
do_not_claim: Question silent-preselect (locked dual-cite); Tidwell Good Defaults as a merge. Placeholder-as-hint as a new Polar row (skipped). Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.inputs.good_defaults_smart_prefills`.
